answer.how_to_obtain_criteria: Humana utilizes MCG™ Care Guidelines (formerly Milliman Care Guidelines) under corporate licensure to perform medical necessity reviews for musculoskeletal procedures like total shoulder replacements. Because MCG guidelines are proprietary third-party clinical criteria, Humana does not publish them on a public web page. According to Humana's guidelines and provider manual, members or their representatives can request a copy of the specific clinical criteria applied to their case, either verbally or in writing, by contacting Humana Member Services at 1-800-233-4013 or 1-877-856-5702, or by calling the phone number printed on the back of their member ID card.
answer.notes: Although the exact proprietary MCG text cannot be quoted without active license credentials, standard MCG clinical criteria for Total Shoulder Arthroplasty (CPT 23472) typically require: (1) Severe, persistent shoulder pain that interferes with functional activities of daily living (e.g., sleep, work, or self-care) for at least 3 months; (2) Advanced joint disease confirmed by imaging (e.g., severe osteoarthritis, inflammatory arthropathy, or avascular necrosis of the humeral head); (3) Documented failure of a 3-month trial of conservative non-surgical treatments, which must include active physical therapy, oral medications (such as NSAIDs or analgesics), and therapeutic shoulder injections (unless contraindicated); (4) An intact or reconstructible rotator cuff (for anatomic shoulder replacement).

According to Humana's guidelines and provider manual, members or their representatives can request a copy of the specific clinical criteria applied to their case, either verbally or in writing, by contacting Humana Member Services at 1-800-233-4013 or 1-877-856-5702, or by calling the phone number printed on the back of their member ID card.",

  "notes": "Although the exact proprietary MCG text cannot be quoted without active license credentials, standard MCG clinical criteria for Total Shoulder Arthroplasty (CPT 23472) typically require: (1) Severe, persistent shoulder pain that interferes with functional activities of daily living (e.g., sleep, work, or self-care) for at least 3 months; (2) Advanced joint disease confirmed by imaging (e.g., severe osteoarthritis, inflammatory arthropathy, or avascular necrosis of the humeral head); (3) Documented failure of a 3-month trial of conservative non-surgical treatments, which must include active physical therapy, oral medications (such as NSAIDs or analgesics), and therapeutic shoulder injections (unless contraindicated); (4) An intact or reconstructible rotator cuff (for anatomic shoulder replacement)."
